stem: If an angle \(\alpha\) is divided into two parts A and B such that \(A - B = x\) and \(\tan A\ :\tan B = 2:1,\) then what is \(\sin x\) equal to?
solution:
\(\alpha = A + B\ and\ A - B = x\)\
    \(\Rightarrow A = \frac{\alpha + x}{2}\ and\ B = \frac{\alpha - x}{2}\)\
    Given, \(\frac{\tan A}{\tan B} = \frac{2}{1}\)\
    \(\Rightarrow \frac{\tan\left( \frac{\alpha + x}{2} \right)}{\tan\left( \frac{\alpha - x}{2} \right)} = \frac{2}{1}\)\
    \(\Rightarrow \frac{\sin{\left( \frac{\alpha - x}{2} \right)\cos\left( \frac{\alpha - x}{2} \right)}}{\cos{\left( \frac{\alpha + x}{2} \right)\sin\left( \frac{\alpha - x}{2} \right)}} = \frac{2}{1}\)\
    \(\Rightarrow \frac{\sin\alpha + \sin x}{\sin\alpha - \sin x} = \frac{2}{1} \Rightarrow \sin x = \frac{\sin\alpha}{3}\)
